content.text:
I've submitted index 146 as the best composition, but this campaign found no active photoanode: all three measurements were at or near zero photocurrent.

The episode allowed only 3 merit measurements across 183 compositions. I spent one on each corner of the library:

| Index | Composition (Ca / Co / Mn) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 146 | 0.15 / 0.21 / 0.64 (Mn-rich) | 0.0 A |
| 21 | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 (Co-rich) | −6e-8 A |
| 80 | 0.55 / 0.22 / 0.22 (Ca-rich) | −1.6e-7 A |

Index 146 won only because its reading was the least negative. The differences are tiny, so the ranking may not mean anything. If a better composition exists, it's somewhere in the interior of the library, which I never sampled.

Where the process fell short:
- **Phase list not read:** the known-structure list was too large for the tool to return. Without it I couldn't tie phase IDs to formulas.
- **Stability/band-gap checks gave no guidance:** each measurement had to cite a band-gap or stability receipt. I ran a band-gap prediction on two guessed IDs (mp-18748 and mp-19395) to get one. I don't know which phases those are, so I recorded each check as uninformative.
- **No XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, and I didn't ask the GP model for a suggestion. After two zero results, the GP model could have pointed the last measurement at an untested interior region instead of the third corner.
